tests.implementation_requirement: Compile point, line, text, column, and area geoms over a Table with computed fields, cartesian bounds, labels, and title to Plotly.
Render a ggplot scatter Manhattan chart from a MatrixTable rows Table with locus x and -log10(p) y, preserving chromosome tick labels 1–22, X, Y.
Grouped histogram must produce five traces and exact bin centers for stack/identity and dodge positions.
A bar geom with 30 distinct Table groups must create 30 Plotly traces.
Compile a ribbon geom using Table expressions as x, ymin, and ymax.
A discrete color scale over 20 Table groups must assign 20 distinct colors.
Manual color scale must use precisely the supplied red and blue colors across grouped points.
Weighted geom_bar over indexed Table arrays must produce bar heights [8,9,5,6].
facet_wrap on a Table group field must produce two Plotly facet annotations.

Deferred by user direction: this test reads 56 legacy Hail Table resources and compares projected all-values data. It is not a requirement for the current Vortex/Iceberg implementation; legacy-format decoding will be addressed later.
Grouped row/column aggregations may index sibling MatrixTable row/column/entry data and must match explicit expected keyed Table results, including globals and aggregation expression scope.
Grouped rows must support sequential row/entry aggregations, fixed-index references to a sibling MatrixTable, result() materialization, and exact rows/entries Table schema and values.
Grouped columns must support sequential column/entry aggregations, fixed-index references to sibling MatrixTable entries, result() materialization, and exact rows/entries Table schema and values.

Check globals literal values through both MatrixTable.annotate_globals and Table.annotate_globals: integers, NaN/infinities, floats, and nested arrays/structs must evaluate to their typed Python values.
For an in-memory and re-read 10x10 MatrixTable, head(1) and head(100) must produce correct row counts via count_rows and forced row count.
After filtering away the first half of a 20-row MatrixTable with empty leading partitions, write/read then head(1/100) must report 1/10 rows.
MatrixTable.head(1, 2) must retain one row and two columns.
MatrixTable.head(1, None) must retain one row and all ten columns.
MatrixTable.head(None, 1) must retain all ten rows and one column.
For an in-memory and re-read 10x10 MatrixTable, tail(1) and tail(100) must produce correct row counts via count_rows and forced row count.
After filtering away the first half of a 20-row MatrixTable with empty leading partitions, write/read then tail(1/100) must report 1/10 rows.
MatrixTable.tail must independently honor row and column limits: (1,2), (1,None), (None,1) give dimensions (1,2), (1,10), (10,1).
After removing the final column, tail(n,m).entries() must collect the exact Cartesian suffix row/column coordinates for row-only, column-only, and combined limits.
Row and column scan counts must stay attached to the expected suffix when taking a 10x11 MatrixTable tail; entries aggregate to coordinates (i,j) with i=20..29, j=29..39.
aggregate_cols(collect(col_idx)) must follow original column order before keying (after choose_cols: [0,1,2]) and chosen physical order once col keys are removed ([2,1,0]).
On rows() of a Balding-Nichols MatrixTable, Table.aggregate(counter(locus.in_x_nonpar())) must count Boolean locus classes.
Selecting nested entry fields must project them into top-level fields; a derived bc expression must equal the previously computed foo in entries().
Column annotation aggregations over entry fields, row/column indices and globals must produce the asserted col struct for column 3.
Grouping columns by a Boolean group and aggregating entries must produce exact row/group sum values, retain globals, and key the result by row_idx and group.
Grouping rows by a Boolean group and aggregating entries must produce exact column/group sums, retain globals, and key by group and col_idx.
collect_cols_by_key must collect exploded column values into ordered arrays and carry entry values into corresponding arrays for every row/column pair.
MatrixTable row semi/anti joins against compatible single- and compound-key Tables must retain/remove expected rows; incompatible or empty Table keys raise the asserted ValueError.
MatrixTable column semi/anti joins against compatible single- and compound-key Tables must retain/remove expected columns; incompatible or empty Table keys raise ValueError.
MatrixTable row/column indexing from derived row and column Tables must annotate matching values and support tuple keys, string casts, and all-row/all-column checks.
Rows/cols Table indexing by expanded key fields must match indexing by the key struct; MatrixTable index_rows/index_cols and entry lookup must agree on equivalent key forms.
A MatrixTable row lookup into a keyed Table with all_matches=True must return all preceding index values for each row.
union_rows must accept differing column schemas and globals and concatenate row counts to 20.
Adding row and column indices to an imported MatrixTable must assign consecutive indices in the materialized rows() and cols() Tables while retaining requested partition count.
Annotating MatrixTable rows from Table lookup by a computed integer key must return values matching locus-position parity.
Table indexing by two computed MatrixTable row keys must return the value encoding parity of locus position and DP; assert across rows().
After exploding a duplicate row-key component, keyed Table lookup must yield the mapped value for the matching key and missing values for other keys.
Matrix row keys indexing a Table keyed by integer intervals must attach the containing interval row or missing result according to half-open interval boundaries.
Interval Table lookup with all_matches=True must return each matching interval value, sorted, with exact match count determined by distance to the nearest ten boundary.
MatrixTable entry self-indexing by row/column keys must preserve entry dtype and reproduce every entry value after column reordering.
Entry lookup in a one-cell MatrixTable must broadcast its foo value to every entry indexed by computed row/column keys.
Entry lookup from a filtered MatrixTable must produce defined scaled values only at retained even row/even column coordinates and missing elsewhere.
MatrixTable.entries() must expose row/column keys and annotated entry fields for all 100 cells with x=row_idx+col_idx.
entries() must preserve documented row-major ordering under original, no-column-key, no-row-key, and no-row-key-only variants.
Entries materialization must work when the row key field order differs from the selected row field order.
After filtering a 10-column MatrixTable to three columns, entries().collect() must return 30 cells.
Converting row, column, and entry structs to fields through rows(), cols(), and entries() must preserve equality of nested/original fields, including missing GT.
MatrixTable.from_rows_table must reconstruct the row-only equivalent of the source MatrixTable after globals, entries, and columns are removed.
After MatrixTable write, its stored cols Table must equal mt.cols() after dropping its key.
After MatrixTable write, its stored rows Table must equal mt.rows() including a global annotation.
After MatrixTable write, its stored globals Table must equal mt.globals_table() including mixed-typed globals.
MatrixTable read with two adjacent row intervals must preserve interval partition selection (2 partitions by default, 3 with filtering) and match equivalent row filtering.
Imported VCF MatrixTable written/re-read with two locus intervals must select two partitions and equal filtering the source by the same disjoint locus ranges.
Indexed MatrixTable reads with several intervals contained within the same or multiple source partitions must retain exactly one or three partitions.
For every backend-supported codec, write/read the rows() Table from an imported MatrixTable and preserve Table equality.
After split_multi_hts and MatrixTable write/read, the stored rows Table, source rows(), and restored rows() must be equal.
range_matrix_table(100,10) must have exact row/column counts; entries().add_index() must assign index equal to 10*row_idx+col_idx.
After adding row/column annotations then filtering entries by (row*col)%4, every materialized entry must satisfy the predicate.
A missing Boolean filter removes all rows, columns, or entries in the corresponding MatrixTable axis.
entries() must order entry field collects by sorted row and column keys, and take(1) must return the first value.
rows() must order rows by row key while preserving original row_idx field values, for collect and take.
Table.order_by accepts a string or asc field and sorts ascending; desc sorts descending.
Table.order_by must sort using a computed negative key expression.
Table.order_by on interval fields must use interval ordering including endpoint inclusion/exclusion distinctions.
range_matrix_table must produce empty globals/entries, typed row/col index schemas and default row/column keys; rows() and cols() collect consecutive indices.
MatrixTable.make_table must flatten entry fields into column-named fields, retain row key and produce exact Table rows.
make_table must retain the source rows Table when row fields and random entry fields are present and flattened into columns.
Table.aggregate with agg.explode over arrays must collect present elements from nonempty, empty, missing arrays and missing elements while ignoring empty/missing arrays.

Table.aggregate(call_stats) must be callable over phased, unphased, haploid, and missing calls and produce the assigned AC/AF/AN/homozygote-count values; note the test passes the actual Table as assertTrue's condition and the expected Table only as its message, so it does not compare the values.
MatrixTable row HWE aggregation, for one- and two-sided tests, must match expected heterozygote frequencies/p-values for five variants and return p=0.5 with NaN frequency for a monomorphic row.
The scalar hardy_weinberg_test function must equal the MatrixTable row aggregation for the same call_stats-derived counts in both one- and two-sided modes.
Writing a zero-row MatrixTable with no row partitions and reading it with rows dropped must preserve MatrixTable equality.
Matrix row distinct-join semantics must preserve matching nonmissing keys and emit missing joined fields for null keys in exact row order.
Table.index with a MatrixTable row key, one key field, nonkey fields, and a point interval key must return exact rows and reject incompatible compound-key arity.
For compound row keys, Table.index must accept matching component arguments, reject incomplete/incompatible key forms, and distinguish point intervals from interval keys over structs.
Matrix entry expressions may combine literals with joined column, row, and entry lookups and lazily selected globals/row/col/entry structs; the resulting MatrixTable count must execute.
localize_entries(None,None) must produce a Table equal to rows(), dropping entry and column-localized fields.
When entry array localization is disabled, localize_entries must retain globals/rows exactly after selecting globals.
localize_entries must pack per-row entry arrays and the columns array into the exact Table schema, row names, values, and globals.
Writing the same MatrixTable three times via experimental.write_matrix_tables must return paths whose re-read MatrixTables all equal the input.
MatrixTable.write(_partitions=intervals) must write exactly the requested row partitions, preserve MatrixTable equality, and support intervals outside data and disjoint subsets.
The nested partition-write helper must construct interval specs, write/read MatrixTables, assert partition count equals interval count, and preserve the expected full or filtered MatrixTable.
Partitioned MatrixTable writes must coerce locus intervals, retain only covered rows, use one output partition, and equal filter_intervals.
MatrixTable.write must fail on an existing path by default and succeed when overwrite=True.
Legacy required-globals Table and MatrixTable resources must be readable and force-countable.
Native MatrixTable write/read of a range dataset must preserve exact MatrixTable equality.
Grouping rows after filtering out every entry must still produce one grouped row and an entries Table row with a zero count.
Grouping columns after filtering out every entry must still produce one grouped column and an entries Table row with a zero count.
Table filtering by a locus.position expression must return the expected row with GRCh37 locus contig and position.
After variant-QC filtering and sampling a MatrixTable, row semi-join and HWE PCA must execute on the selected genotype data.
A row scan collected after changing row keys must follow the prior reversed-key order; re-keying back must preserve expected per-row prefixes.
The all-values MatrixTable helper fixture must survive MatrixTable native write/read with exact schema and data equality.
Reading a 3-partition MatrixTable with _n_partitions=10 must expose ten output partitions.
Filtering generated MatrixTable loci to a contig absent from the reference genome must return zero rows.
MatrixFilterRows with a random condition must materialize without consumer randomness and preserve globally unique random IDs at row/column/entry scopes.
MatrixFilterEntries with a random condition must materialize entries and maintain globally unique random IDs across all scopes.
MatrixMapGlobals with random global value must execute entries and keep random IDs unique across scopes.
MatrixMapGlobals without randomness must preserve unique IDs across all scopes and expose the expected IR node.
MatrixFilterCols with a random condition must execute entries and preserve unique random IDs across scopes.
MatrixRepartition must appear in the IR when lowering is supported and preserve globally unique random IDs.
MatrixRowsHead must appear in IR for a row head and preserve random ID uniqueness.
MatrixColsHead must appear in IR for a column head and preserve random ID uniqueness.
MatrixRowsTail must appear in IR for a row tail and preserve random ID uniqueness.
MatrixColsTail must appear in IR for a column tail and preserve random ID uniqueness.
Unlocalizing a Table with entry/global arrays into a MatrixTable must create CastTableToMatrix IR and preserve unique random IDs.
Annotating MatrixTable rows from a keyed Table with duplicate interval-like row keys must create MatrixAnnotateRowsTable IR and retain globally unique random IDs.
Annotating MatrixTable columns from a keyed Table must create MatrixAnnotateColsTable IR and retain globally unique random IDs.
MatrixTable.rename must produce MatrixRename IR and preserve globally unique random IDs.
Tuple-valued column annotations must remain indexable after explode and drop; cols().collect() must execute.
Sampling the MatrixTable.entries() Table at fraction 0.5 must be executable and force-countable.
Checkpointing random and numeric entry fields with unstable struct-of-arrays encoding must write EStructOfArrays metadata and re-read equal to the standard encoding.
MatrixTable.from_parts with 2x1 nested entry arrays, after row/column selections, must emit exactly two entries with correct row_idx, col_idx and values.
Plot a Table field’s empirical CDF. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Grouped histogram must produce five traces and exact bin centers for stack/identity and dodge positions.
Plot the estimated density of a Table field. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Plot the smoothed density of a Table field. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Plot cumulative Table-field histograms with explicit and automatic bins. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Plot a 2D histogram of Table field idx against idx squared. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Plot Table field idx against its square. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Render a joint plot for two Table expressions. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Render a QQ plot of the Table expression idx/100. The test asserts that plotting executes without error.
Build a Manhattan plot from an indexed Table derived from a Balding-Nichols MatrixTable and preserve canonical GRCh37 chromosome tick labels 1–22, X, Y.

For Manhattan/scatter/joint/QQ functions over an indexed MatrixTable rows Table, collect_all=True and n_divisions=0 must raise ValueError; n_divisions=None emits no warning unless collect_all=True, which warns with the plot name.
Segment reference blocks by a keyed interval Table across chr22; write/re-read as MatrixTable, verify every segment’s END stays inside its interval, and preserve per-sample covered bases.

Given a Table of two parsed locus intervals and GQ/DP thresholds, VDS interval_coverage must produce asserted interval sizes, threshold counts/fractions, and DP sums; mean_dp values are calculated for comparison with pytest.approx but that comparison result is not asserted.
Convert a Table of sample/interval/depth rows into a MatrixTable and infer autosomal/X/Y mean depth and ploidy for XX and XY samples using normalization contig 20.
From synthetic reference/empty-variant MatrixTables built from Table data, infer XX/XY sex-chromosome ploidies from GRCh37 calling intervals using normalization contig 22.

Build reference and variant MatrixTables through Table-to-Matrix fixtures, then impute sample sex-chromosome ploidy from VariantDataset depth over disjoint autosomal/X/Y intervals with use_variant_dataset=True. Collect exact Table rows for sample_xx (autosomal/X/Y depth 5/5/0 and X/Y ploidy 2/0) and sample_xy (5/3/2 and 1.2/0.8); this requires VDS and Matrix algorithms beyond the Table engine.
VDS interval filtering must accept an interval-keyed Table with split_reference_blocks=True and match list-based filtering in dense form, with both reference and variant loci in range.
Default VDS interval filtering must accept an interval-keyed Table, match list-based filtering after densification, and restrict variant loci to the requested interval.
Densify a filtered chr22 VDS to MatrixTable while preserving variant rows and recoverable entries; assert exact reference-block missingness and LGT/LA/GQ/DP values for listed sample/locus pairs.

When reference blocks contain haploid calls, densification must preserve variant rows, recoverable entries, missingness and expected haploid versus diploid LGT values at listed chr22 sample/locus pairs.

Merge reference blocks using GQ equality and configured LEN/MIN_DP/N_BLOCKS reducers; preserve sample QC coverage bins and total block count/base count, then split_multi must rename GT/LGT fields as expected.
VDS interval filtering from an interval-keyed Table built from the first ten variant rows must retain exactly those variant rows.
